auth.quote: Both basic and bearer authentication are supported.
It is up to your application to generate bearer tokens via your SSO provider.
The Aura API uses OAuth 2.0 for API authentication.
Access tokens are temporary and expire after one hour.

access.quote: No credit card or other payment method required
All tiers can create Aura API credentials.

api.quote: The Query API allows to execute Cypher statements against a Neo4j server through HTTP requests.
The Aura API allows you to programmatically perform actions on your Aura instances

mcp.quote: Neo4j MCP for Aura is a hosted MCP server for your Aura instances.
MCP for Aura is available for Free, Professional, and Business Critical tier instances.

buildability.quote: No credit card or other payment method required
Both basic and bearer authentication are supported.

uncertain.api_breadth: The data-plane Query API has only a handful of endpoints (implicit query plus explicit transactions), but it runs arbitrary Cypher. The Aura management API v1 has about 26 operations (counted from aura_api_spec_v1.yaml) and v2beta1 has about 95 (beta). moderate reflects GA operations; broad is defensible if beta management endpoints or Cypher's expressiveness count.
uncertain.auth_primary: There is no user-delegated OAuth authorization-code flow. Database access is username/password (Basic) or an SSO bearer token; the Aura API uses OAuth2 client credentials (client id/secret exchanged for a 1-hour token). For a multi-user toolkit, Basic (URI + user + password) is the realistic primary.
uncertain.mcp: The MCP for Aura docs page does not say whether it is preview or GA. A Neo4j blog post ('Introducing MCP for Aura') exists but I did not open it.

notes: AuraDB Free is $0 with no credit card, and the Query API and the instance-management API are both listed as included on every tier, Free included. Neo4j has three MCP offerings: (1) the hosted 'MCP for Aura', a per-instance URL https://<INSTANCE_ID>.mcp-instances.neo4j.io that requires 'Tool authentication' enabled in the Aura console; (2) the official local neo4j/mcp (Go binary, PyPI neo4j-mcp-server, latest v2.1.2 on 2026-11-23; tools get-schema, read-cypher, write-cypher, list-gds-procedures); (3) the separate Neo4j Labs servers in neo4j-contrib/mcp-neo4j (cypher, memory, aura-manager, data-modeling), which are not the official product. The hint URL neo4j.com/docs/api returned 404. Bolt drivers (a binary protocol) are the main client path but are not a separate api_style enum.
